record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can the best known deterministic space upper bound for randomized space BPSPACE(s) be improved?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Improve the deterministic space complexity of BPSPACE(s).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a space-constructible function $s: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $s(n) \geq \log n$, let $\mathrm{BPSPACE}(s)$ denote the class of languages decided by randomized Turing machines that, on inputs of length $n$, use $O(s(n))$ workspace, halt in finite time on every random-string branch, and err with probability at most $1/3$. Let $\mathrm{DSPACE}(t)$ denote the class of languages decided by deterministic Turing machines using $O(t(n))$ workspace.

The Saks–Zhou theorem gives the inclusion $\mathrm{BPSPACE}(s) \subseteq \mathrm{DSPACE}(s^{3/2})$, and subsequent work has obtained the slightly stronger inclusion $\mathrm{BPSPACE}(s) \subseteq \mathrm{DSPACE}(s^{3/2}/\sqrt{\log s})$.

Problem: Improve the deterministic space complexity of $\mathrm{BPSPACE}(s)$. That is, exhibit a function $t(s) = o(s^{3/2}/\sqrt{\log s})$ such that
$$\mathrm{BPSPACE}(s) \subseteq \mathrm{DSPACE}(t(s)),$$
or, ideally, prove that $\mathrm{BPSPACE}(s) \subseteq \mathrm{DSPACE}(s^{1+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$ (or even $\mathrm{BPSPACE}(s) \subseteq \mathrm{DSPACE}(s)$).
artifact.status_search_result: The Saks–Zhou bound $\mathrm{BPSPACE}(s) \subseteq \mathrm{DSPACE}(s^{3/2})$ from 1999 remained the best known for over two decades. A recent improvement by Hoza (APPROX/RANDOM 2021) achieves $\mathrm{DSPACE}(s^{3/2}/\sqrt{\log s})$ using weighted pseudorandom generators, but this is only a sub-polynomial improvement. Reducing the exponent below $3/2$ (and, in particular, proving $\mathrm{BPL} \subseteq \mathrm{L}$) remains a major open problem in complexity theory.

status_evidence.title: Better Pseudodistributions and Derandomization for Space-Bounded Computation
status_evidence.snippet: BPSPACE(S) ⊆ DSPACE(S^{3/2}/√log S) via weighted PRGs.
status_evidence.claim: Best known bound slightly improves Saks–Zhou by a √log s factor; improving the 3/2 exponent remains open.

status_evidence.title: BPL ⊆ SC and the Saks-Zhou theorem (lecture notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Saks–Zhou gives BPSPACE(s) ⊆ DSPACE(s^{3/2}); improving this is a central open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The Saks–Zhou exponent 3/2 has not been improved beyond logarithmic factors.
